title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: Notice Windows by Kind of Loss
content:
Written notice of loss under `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims` must reach the line within a window that depends on the kind of loss and on whether the loss could be seen at delivery.

## Which window applies

| Kind of loss | Recorded as apparent at delivery | Tier's visible loss period | Window |
|---|---|---|---|
| delay loss | either | any | the delay loss period |
| any other kind | no | any | the hidden loss period |
| any other kind | yes | above 0 | the visible loss period |
| any other kind | yes | 0 | no dated window |

## Counting a dated window

The last day of the window is the cover's delivery date carried forward by the window's number of days, counted on calendar dates. Notice dated on the last day itself still counts as in time; notice dated any later is rejected as out of time.

## Visible loss under a zero period

Under a tier whose visible loss period is 0, a visible loss of any kind except delay loss has no dated window. What such a loss requires is a notation on the delivery receipt, and a notice recorded as apparent at delivery carries that notation. Such a notice is therefore never rejected as out of time.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical windows and dates)

- A hidden loss under a tier with a hypothetical hidden loss period of 10 days, delivered on 3 July: the last day is 13 July. A notice dated 13 July is in time; one dated 14 July is out of time.
- A visible physical damage loss under a tier with a hypothetical visible loss period of 5 days, delivered on 28 September: the last day is 3 October. A notice dated 4 October is out of time.
- A visible wet damage loss under a tier whose visible loss period is 0, noticed forty days after delivery: no dated window applies, so the notice is not out of time.
- A delay loss recorded as apparent at delivery: the delay loss period governs, whatever the visible loss period.
